newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul prosecutors seek arrest of MPs over Hanbo - TV.
newsitem.headline: Seoul prosecutors seek arrest of MPs over Hanbo - TV.

text.p: South Korean state prosecutors plan to seek arrest warrants for two members of parliament, including a close associate of President Kim Young-sam, over a loan scandal, Yonhap Television News reported on Tuesday.

A prosecution official told Reuters prosecutors were questioning Hong In-gil, a senior official at the presidential Blue House until last year, and Chung Jae-chull in connection with huge loans to Hanbo Steel Co but no decision had been made on whether to seek arrest warrants.

On Monday the prosecutors summoned Hong and Chung, one of top three officials at the ruling New Korea Party, to determine if they accepted kickbacks from Hanbo Steel and pressured bankers into offering loans to the company.
"The prosecution plans to seek arrest warrants for the two lawmakers today," the television reported.

The two are the first politicians to be probed over loans totalling five trillion won ($5.8 billion) provided to Hanbo Steel, South Korea's second largest steelmaker, before it was declared insolvent on January 23.
President Kim last month ordered a probe into the loans. He has called the scandal a typical example of corruption.
